target_customer: Infusion clinics (rheumatology, headache, other biologic administering practices) that pay for prior authorization and benefits investigation work
problem: Biologics cost $80K to $150K+ per patient per year and are often denied; paper and spreadsheet workflows leave clinics unreimbursed. Janeen handles benefits investigation, prior authorization submission, insurer calls and appeals end to end.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services per clinic, pricing not found; free Formulary Navigator tool as lead generation
product_category: Prior authorization and benefits investigation automation for infusion clinics

founders.name: Meng Fei Shen
education: Yale (met co-founder there; no degree listed)
founders.background_notes: YC page: quit big tech to work as a medical assistant; runs a 120+ person music collective in SF.

founders.name: Christina Lee Huang
education: Yale (met co-founder there; no degree listed)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes her as a former patient who fought payers for her own biologic treatments; title not given there (aggregators say CTO).

competitors.name: SamaCare
competitors.traction_then: reported $6.2B in specialty drug prior authorizations processed in 2025 (company claim)

competitors.name: Plenful
competitors.what: Intake authorization suite that extracts referral data, verifies benefits and fills payer forms
competitors.traction_then: claims over 75 percent reduction in manual effort

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping drug, payer and diagnosis rules, form filling, insurer calls and appeals needs integrations and rule data but uses mostly standard automation and LLM tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Payer rule data and clinic workflow integration help, but SamaCare, Plenful and others sell similar products, and Innovaccer entered infusion in July 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Innovaccer configured its Gravity platform for infusion access in July 2026 (after founding).

market_need_then: The company cites 37 percent annual insurer denial of specialty medications and clinics paying for drugs upfront; the founder's patient experience and live clinic use in California and Nevada support need (company claims of 50 percent lower denials).

branding.domain_note: Uses janeen.care; the earlier name was Ruma Care (rumacare.com per aggregators).

identity.mascot_or_character: The product is personified as a capable teammate named 'she'
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, confident and practical ('She knows everything', 'their afternoons back')

branding.brand_signature: A named, personified assistant ('Janeen') rather than a software label

rebrands.why: not stated; YC page says 'formerly Ruma Care'

branding.community_and_virality: Free Formulary Navigator tool as a shareable asset; no fan or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A human name humanizes the product, but the rename is recent, the old name still appears in testimonials and URLs, and no independent brand press exists.

outcome_analysis: Janeen, formerly Ruma Care, is a Winter 2026 company with five people and reported live use in infusion clinics in California and Nevada. Founder market fit is notable since a co-founder is a former biologics patient. Funding is not verified from a primary source and larger vendors are entering infusion, so the outcome is open.
notes: Unverified funding: VCBacked, Employbl and Caplight list a $2.0M pre-seed (Caplight dates it 2026-03-24) with Y Combinator, Flybridge and Rebel Fund, while Standout lists $2.5M seed; all aggregators, no company or press confirmation, so no round recorded. The janeen.care page does not mention the rename; the YC page says formerly Ruma Care. YC's batch listing is W26 and Ruma Care's YC page title carries that name.
